Hi Alice — thanks for the template and the timeline. Per Aditya's Qs: for your review we will assume the following definitions so the mapping is unambiguous:

- Hosted (Redwood Managed, multi-tenant runtime): Redwood manages the control plane and runtime. Customer data is isolated logically; compute runs on shared pools. Redwood controls key management for platform-level keys; customers can bring their own keys for specific optional features via KMS integrations. Network: outbound egress managed by Redwood; no VPC peering. Logs: audit and usage logs are stored by Redwood; retention defaults are 90 days but can be extended via add-on.

- Dedicated (Redwood Managed, single-tenant compute): Reserved GPU pools for a single customer. Control plane remains Redwood-managed unless customer purchases Private variant. Network: optional VPC peering for egress and restricted ingress; we support customer NAT + peering. Keys: Redwood hosts keys unless a customer-supplied KMS integration is configured; customer has isolation at compute layer. Logs: per-tenant logs retained per contract; we can push logs to customer SIEM via syslog/forwarding.

- Private (Customer Managed control plane / on-prem): Customer runs the control plane in their VPC or in their datacenter (on-prem bundle). Customer is responsible for network perimeter, key management (HSM/KMS), and retention policies. Redwood provides the runtime software, deployment automation, and optional managed services under an enterprise agreement. Audit evidence: in this mode, Redwood provides deployment manifests, install guides, and access logs captured by the customer environment.

Attached is a compact deployment-matrix CSV and a network-diagram for your binder. Below are suggested short statements you can paste into SIG answers for each responsibility area (we kept them intentionally concise for the SIG format):

- Network perimeter: Hosted: Redwood — controls perimeter for shared runtime. Dedicated: Shared responsibility — Redwood controls compute perimeter; customer controls VPC if peering enabled. Private: Customer — controls perimeter in their VPC/datacenter.
- Key management: Hosted: Redwood (customer optional BYOK). Dedicated: Redwood by default; BYOK via KMS supported. Private: Customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Audit logs & retention: Hosted: Redwood retains audit logs (default 90 days); customer can request exports. Dedicated: Redwood retains per-tenant logs; can forward to customer SIEM. Private: Customer retains logs in their environment; Redwood provides guidance and export hooks.
- Data persistence & backups: Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood manages backups; data encrypted at rest. Private: Customer manages backups per their policy.
- Access control & admin: Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood supports RBAC and SAML/SCIM integrations; Redwood manages platform-level admin. Private: Customer integrates with their identity provider and manages admin lifecycle.

If this level of language works, we’ll populate the SIG spreadsheet with exact cell answers and return by Monday EOD.

Thanks,
